title: epan: Optimize ws_label_strcpy and dissect_per_boolean performance
description:
ws_label_strcpy: Add a fast path for runs of printable ASCII (0x20-0x7E) that uses memcpy instead of per-character processing. This eliminates per-byte UTF-8 length lookups, g_ascii_isprint table checks, and redundant NUL-termination on every character. The common case (flags == 0) is separated into its own loop to avoid checking FORMAT_LABEL_REPLACE_SPACE in the hot path.

dissect_per_boolean: Simplify bit extraction to a single branchless shift-and-mask expression. Add early return when hf_index \<= 0 to skip string formatting overhead during non-tree passes.

Performance results (NGAP 1000 packets, tshark -2 -V): 

* Before: 1.62s avg
* After: 1.51s avg (\~7% overall speedup)

perf profile (self time): 

* ws_label_strcpy: 9.9% -\> 5.0% (50% reduction)
* dissect_per_boolean: 1.82% -\> 1.57% (14% reduction)

AI-Assisted: yes (Kiro)

notes.body: Been thinking about using tvb get bits function in this dissector. Would that be an option here?

It's not a good option for this case. Here's why:

tvb_get_bits8(tvb, offset, 1) would be worse because:

1. More overhead — It calls \_tvb_get_bits64() which does a DISSECTOR_ASSERT, then computes octet_offset = bit_offset \>\> 3, required_bits_in_first_octet = 8 - (bit_offset % 8), a branch, a mask table lookup via bit_mask8\[\], and calls tvb_get_uint8() internally anyway.
2. The current code is already minimal — tvb_get_uint8(tvb, offset\>\>3) followed by a single shift-and-mask is essentially doing the same thing in 2 instructions that tvb_get_bits8 does in \~10+ with function call overhead.
3. No bounds checking benefit — tvb_get_uint8 already does bounds checking on the tvb, so you don't gain safety.

The only scenario where tvb_get_bits functions make sense is when you're extracting multi-bit fields that span byte boundaries (e.g., 5-bit integers). For a single boolean (1 bit, guaranteed within one byte), the direct approach is both clearer and faster.
Do we think that this code is truly self-commenting enough to remove the comments here and elsewhere?
No, the comments are still valid. Will restore them
